paragraphs: 6 former Mustangs appeared in professional games on Wednesday for 6 clubs across 3 levels, with Brooks Lee producing the night's most notable performance.

Brooks Lee's home run — his 21th of the season came in the first inning on a 1-0 93 mph four-seam fastball from J.T. Ginn. The swing moved the score from 0-0 to 1-0. Statcast measured the ball at 104.5 mph off the bat, a 28-degree launch angle, 373 feet.
Brooks Lee went 1-for-4, 1 home run, 1 RBI, 1 run scored.
He batted second and started at third base.

Bryce Warrecker came on in relief for Hudson Valley Renegades in the top of the fifth with two outs. He worked 2 1/3 innings, allowing 1 hit and 0 earned runs, with 1 walk and 1 strikeout. One of his strikeouts came in the sixth on a 1-2 pitch, when he put away Aidan Smith. Hudson Valley Renegades fell to Brooklyn Cyclones, 5-11.
Alejandro Garza went 1-for-4, 1 stolen base for Hill City Howlers at Single-A. He batted first and started at second base. Hill City Howlers fell to Kannapolis Cannon Ballers, 0-5.

Taylor Dollard started on the mound for Everett AquaSox. He worked 1 1/3 innings, allowing 0 hits and 0 earned runs, with 1 walk and 1 strikeout. One of his strikeouts came in the first on a 1-2 pitch, when he put away Cam Maldonado. Everett AquaSox beat Eugene Emeralds, 11-6.
Ryan Stafford went 1-for-1 for Frederick Keys at High-A. He batted ninth and appeared at PH. Frederick Keys beat Asheville Tourists, 3-2.

Bryan Woo started on the mound for Seattle Mariners. He worked 4.0 innings, allowing 5 hits and 6 earned runs, with 1 walk and 5 strikeouts. One of his strikeouts came in the first on a 0-2 98 mph four-seam fastball, when he put away Trea Turner. Seattle Mariners fell to Philadelphia Phillies, 0-6.
title: Brooks Lee comes through late with a go-ahead hit
